_README: Index/ETF WEIGHTING METHODOLOGY, keyed by the returns-block display ticker.
Rendered as a parenthetical on every returns-block row so the cross-index
comparisons in the digest are interpretable (an equal-weighted biotech basket
and a cap-weighted one are not the same read).
VALUES:
a string  -> rendered verbatim inside the row's parenthetical, e.g.
`XBI` (Biotech, equal-weighted).
null      -> DELIBERATELY unlabeled. Use for instruments where 'weighting'
is not a meaningful concept (a single spot asset, a bond yield,
a currency basket) or where the methodology could not be
established confidently. null is an explicit decision, not a
gap -- see the validator note below.
NOT a free-text field. Three categories are in use, and price-weighted is a
real third category -- do NOT collapse it into the equal/cap binary:
'market-cap weighted'  (includes float-adjusted and modified/capped cap
weighting -- the cap-vs-equal distinction is what
matters at a glance, capping nuance is not)
'equal-weighted'       (includes S&P 'modified equal weight' Select Industry
indices)
'price-weighted'       (the DJIA family -- weight follows share price, not
market cap)
EVERY ticker in the returns-block source files must have a key here, string
or null. main() validates this at startup and prints a [WARN] for any gap, so
a newly added ticker cannot silently ship unlabeled (no-silent-failures).
Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and are ignored by the loader.
Added 2026-07-19 alongside IHF.
